newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on FOMC woes, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on FOMC woes, profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed moderately lower Thursday after zizagging through the session on changing fortunes on Wall Street and jitters ahead of the May 20 U..S Federal Reserve meeting to review U.S. interest rates.
"It looks very cautious ahead of the FOMC (Fed) meeting and I think the majority are calling each other's bluff," an analyst said, who asked not to be identified.
The leading IPC share index ended down 7.00 points, or 0.18 percent, at 3,887.20.
The analyst added that first-quarter public finance data released in the -morning failed to produce a lasting recovery in share prices.
"The market did not react as expected to the economic data," he said.

Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz unveiled Mexico's public finance balance sheet for the first quarter. Among other data, he said Mexico posted a public sector surplus of 8.991 billion pesos ($1.14 billion).
Ortiz told journalists separately he expected that first quarter GDP growth was between 4.5 percent and 5.0 percent.
A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses shows an average forecast increase of 5.12 percent for first quarter GDP, which is due to be announced next Monday.
Dealers said stocks were hit by profit-taking.
Trading volume was much reduced from Wednesday's session at 77.2 million shares.
Mexico's three biggest financial groups, Bancomer, Banacci and Serfin, shrugged off the downtrend among blue chips and put in a strong performance.
One trader suggested the three banks all creditors of Grupo Sidek, benefitted from speculation the troubled conglomerate has reached a deal to restructure its debt.

Bancomer ended up seven centavos (1 cent) at 2.91 pesos (37 cents), Banacci climbed 28 centavos (4 cents) to 17.80 pesos ($2.25), while Serfin gained five centavos (less than 1 cent) to 2.55 pesos (32 cents). Grupo Sidek B shares meanwhile gained four centavos (less than 1 cent) to 75 centavos (10 cents).
"Sidek will hold a shareholders' assembly on May 30, and that is why the stock is heating up," an analyst said.
Telmex weighed most on the downside, falling two centavos (less than 1 cent) to 17.14 pesos ($2.17).
On the broad market, 110 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outstripped sliders by 47 to 40.
